connection: Session 20 established bool outcomes for expected service rejections, while ClockEntry protects invalid state with exceptions. This session makes that distinction explicit and verifies the existing contracts with focused tests.
objectives: Distinguish an expected service rejection from a broken ClockEntry invariant.
Verify that TryClockOut returns false when no open entry exists.
Verify that ClockOutEntry and GetDuration throw InvalidOperationException for invalid state.
Write focused tests that preserve each outcome contract.

visuals.title: Expected rejection stays in normal flow
visuals.explanation: TryClockOut returns false when no open entry exists; the caller can branch on that ordinary outcome.

visuals.title: Invalid object state throws
visuals.explanation: ClockOutEntry rejects a second completion, and GetDuration rejects an open entry because neither operation has a valid result.

visuals.title: The method contract communicates the choice
visuals.explanation: bool communicates an expected yes-or-no outcome; InvalidOperationException communicates that the requested operation is invalid for the current state.

visuals.title: Tests preserve both contracts
visuals.explanation: Separate tests prove the false result and each exception without catching failures merely to hide them.

preQuiz.prompt: What should TryClockOut return when no open entry exists?
preQuiz.explanation: Session 20 established this as an expected service rejection.

preQuiz.prompt: Why does GetDuration throw while Clockout is null?
options: An open entry has no completed duration
Nullable analysis requires every method to throw
preQuiz.explanation: The requested value does not exist until clock-out completes the interval.

preQuiz.prompt: What should a validation test assert?
options: The observable return or exception contract
Only that the method was called
preQuiz.explanation: Tests protect behavior callers can rely on.

concept.title: Use normal control flow for expected rejection
paragraphs: TryClockOut returns bool because an employee having no open entry is an ordinary outcome the caller can handle.
The false result does not mean the repository failed. It means the requested use case could not proceed.

concept.title: Use an exception when the object cannot honor the operation
paragraphs: ClockOutEntry cannot complete an entry twice. GetDuration cannot calculate a finished interval while Clockout is null.
Both methods throw InvalidOperationException because the requested operation is invalid for the object's current state.

concept.title: Test each contract directly
paragraphs: A false-result test uses an ordinary assertion. An exception test captures InvalidOperationException and checks the message that explains the violated rule.
Do not catch an exception in production code merely to convert every failure into the same vague result.

lab.objective: Add precise production validation and domain exceptions, then verify invalid behavior with tests.
lab.startingCondition: ClockEntry and services implement valid workflows. Invalid IDs, duplicate completion, and open-entry duration need consistent documented behavior.
steps: Open Domain/Models/ClockEntry.cs and Domain/ClockEntryService.cs. List the three cases to verify: completing an entry twice, requesting duration while an entry is open, and clocking out an employee with no open entry.
For each case, record whether it is an expected not-found result or an invalid operation. Keep this note temporary; the tests will become the permanent specification.
Edit ClockEntry.ClockOutEntry so a second completion throws InvalidOperationException with a message that states the entry is already complete.
Edit ClockEntry.GetDuration so an open entry throws InvalidOperationException with a message that states clock-out is required before duration can be calculated.
Edit ClockEntryService.TryClockOut only if its current bool behavior does not match the established service contract. Do not catch an exception merely to hide it.
Create ClockEntryValidationTests.cs in the Domain.Tests project and declare a public sealed ClockEntryValidationTests class.
Add a Fact test named ClockOutEntry_WhenAlreadyComplete_ThrowsInvalidOperationException and assert both the exception type and its message.
Add a Fact test named GetDuration_WhenEntryIsOpen_ThrowsInvalidOperationException and assert both the exception type and its message.
Add a Fact test named TryClockOut_WhenNoOpenEntryExists_ReturnsFalse using a ClockEntryRepository and ClockEntryService.
Run the focused ClockEntryValidationTests, then run the App's valid workflow and the full PinkMachine19.TimeClock.sln test suite.
lab.expectedBehavior: Valid workflows remain unchanged, invalid states fail precisely, and tests document the contract.
lab.validation: dotnet build PinkMachine19.TimeClock.sln --configuration Release && dotnet test PinkMachine19.TimeClock.sln --configuration Release --no-build

postQuiz.prompt: Why not make TryClockOut throw when no open entry exists?
options: Its Try name and bool return already define an expected rejection contract
Exceptions cannot be used in services
postQuiz.explanation: The current contract lets callers branch without exception handling.

postQuiz.prompt: What breaks if ClockOutEntry silently overwrites Clockout?
options: The original completion time and duration can be corrupted
postQuiz.explanation: The invariant protects recorded time from a second completion.

options: It verifies the failure explains which rule was violated
postQuiz.explanation: Useful messages make failures diagnosable while the type communicates the broad category.

reflections: Which TimeClock outcomes are ordinary enough for bool or nullable returns?
Which ClockEntry operations have no meaningful result in an invalid state?
What behavior belongs in a permanent test rather than a temporary planning comment?
whatBreaks: Removing the false guard from TryClockOut would dereference a missing entry or misreport success. Allowing ClockOutEntry to complete the same entry twice would overwrite recorded state. Allowing GetDuration on an open entry would invent a duration that the object cannot know yet.
summary: TryClockOut returns false for the expected case where an employee has no open entry. ClockEntry throws InvalidOperationException when callers request an invalid state transition or duration. Focused tests make those distinct contracts permanent.
